institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Besides liking Paris, the courses offered at Sciences Po in Paris was in line with my interests, e.g. international development.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I bit confusing, but I figured it out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard to find housing. I used Facebook 'Danskere i Paris' which worked wonders.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive to live in Paris + Check for good metro connections.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No help from Sciences Po and I did not recieve a spot at the Danish House in the Cité. Very late notice of this.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty clear guidelines received via KUmail. A bit stressfull course application process, but the university is changing this.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information sessions, possibility to contact their staff. Quick replies.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was pretty stressfull but I managed as I had prepared at long list of courses in advance. Not able to get all my first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make a list of all the courses you like beforehand. I would say have at least 2 back-ups for each course you're taking. The reg. process is pretty intense (first come/first serve principle)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is more practical than academic. In general really interesting subjects, but very different from KU!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More practical, a lot of practitioners teaching. I really liked it, but sometimes they went off track and did not really follow the readings for class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Food Politics; crisis and transitions
Communicating the Climate Crisis
Social Dimensions of Climate Change
Introduction to African History since 1800
Discrimination and anti-discrimination: Historical, literary and legal interpretations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global Food Politics was really interesting! Communicating the climate crisis was also a fun class where you had to make a 'creative' climate communication product.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I thought I could bike but chose to take the metro. I had to buy the metro card for each month (86 EUR).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More expensive to go out on cafés and restaurants than expected. The Welcome week programme cost 2000 DKK and was not worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not participate in anything, but there were many many options.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I general go to museums, koncerts and markets. If you are under 26 years you can go to all museums in Paris for free.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can do weekend trips, e.g. to Lyon, explore all the farmers markets and flea markets, go to museums or cultural activities (opera, ballets, jazz koncerts, cinema etc.). Eat a lot of good food!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be open and ask people to grab a coffee after class or have lunch together or go to the library together.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like how you say hello and goodbye / have a good day in all stores / cafés etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.) There is a HIGH workload at the University - a lot of exams in each course. Remember to check this before signing up for your course. But the content is not too academically challenging.
2.) The Welcome Programme is not so good. I liked it only because I found some friends I stayed in touch with throughout the semester, but not really value for money.
3.) In general it's a more 'practical' University, differing quite a lot from University of CPH. I liked it,  but had to adjust and found it a bit challenging for what they expected in the exams/papers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really! Just be prepared for a high workload during midterms and finals.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: A lot of new knowledge and friends!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam periods were quite stressfull to be honest.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Depsite high workloads, I believe it was worth it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
